subject: Post-call: model suitability pack & prompt samples requested
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Ali Hassan <ali@papertrail.ai>; PaperTrail Product <product@papertrail.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model suitability pack & prompt samples requested

Hi Ali / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier—great to meet you all. Quick recap and a small request so we can validate model fit and scope an evaluation: 

Recap (50k ft)
- Primary product goal: surface accurate, short-answer explanations for debugging logs and tag root causes.
- Volume: ~7M queries/month initially; 95th perc latency target ~350ms for single-turn answers.
- Data sensitivity: logs contain PII (user IDs, IPs), plus internal error traces; PaperTrail prefers a private deployment or dedicated tenancy.

To move forward with a rapid model suitability assessment we need a small, de-identified prompt pack from you (see ask below). We can then run focused benchmarks and recommend the smallest-sufficient model + quantization profile.

Ask: sample prompt set and redaction guidance
1) 200–500 representative user queries (single-turn) in CSV form: columns: id, timestamp, raw_query, expected_label/answer (if available). We just need examples (not full logs).
2) Highlight 10 high-risk edge cases where privacy or hallucination risk is elevated (short bullet list).
3) Tell us your preferred redaction policy — e.g., remove IPs/UUIDs or replace with tokens like <REDACTED_USER_ID>. If you don’t have one, we can propose a minimal safe default.

What we'll deliver (purview)
- Quick model suitability pack: recommended model variants (cost vs latency), a 20-query micro-benchmark, and qualitative notes about hallucination/error modes.
- Link to the benchmark report and the evaluation harness; we’ll mark anything that needs special handling for the private deployment.

Timelines
- If we get the sample pack by EOD Tues (Sep 3), we can return a suitability pack and benchmark within 5 business days.

Attachments: I included a short template CSV (papertrail_prompt_samples_template.csv) to make the export easier. Also looping Ben and Marissa (ML infra + evaluation) to ensure we capture your constraints.

Thanks—
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Ali Hassan <ali@papertrail.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: PaperTrail Product <product@papertrail.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model suitability pack & prompt samples requested

Connor—

Appreciate the clear recap. Attaching the initial set of examples (papertrail_prompt_samples.csv) and a short internal note on our minimal redaction approach. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The dataset is anonymized per our usual process (user ids replaced with <UID>, IPs removed). We kept timestamps for recency signals.
- Expected answers are noisy; we flagged around ~120 records with human labels.
- Edge cases: included 8 bullets (attached as the final tab in the CSV) — mainly multi-line stack traces, encrypted tokens, and truncated logs that frequently confuse baseline models.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) For the micro-benchmark, do you want us to add a separate column with the ground-truth answer, or is the current label field enough?
2) Any quick do/don'ts for redaction? We prefer to avoid heavy masking because some tokens (like service names) are useful.

We’ll review the proposed redaction defaults if you suggest them. Looking forward to the suitability pack.

—Ali
Head of Product | PaperTrail AI
ali@papertrail.ai

Attachments: papertrail_prompt_samples.csv
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ali Hassan <ali@papertrail.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: model suitability pack & prompt samples requested

Ben / Marissa — forwarding PaperTrail's sample pack. Highlights I pulled out:

- ~320 rows, 120 labeled; labels are concise short answers (1–3 tokens) in many cases.
- Redaction: they replaced user ids with <UID> and removed direct IPs; service names preserved.
- Edge cases list includes: multi-line traces, obfuscated tokens (api_key-like), truncated messages where context is missing.

Initial thoughts (quick skim):
- Likely candidates: redwood-8k-llm-v2 (lower cost, good for short generation) and redwood-xl-16k for cases where we need larger context (stack traces). Recommend quantized q4_0 for the 8k case to cut cost.
- Latency target: we should run a 20-query 95th percentile latency test on dedicated q4 profile to validate the 350ms SLO.
- Quality concerns: hallucinations on truncated logs and overconfident root-cause assertions — we should prioritize precision metrics and a conservative temperature baseline (0.0–0.2) in the first pass.

Requests for evaluation run: 
1) Ben: can your team run the standard micro-benchmark (20 queries) and the 120 labeled examples for accuracy/precision/recall on the two model configs? Use the quantized variant for cost estimates. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-model-eval-harness
2) Marissa: can you draft short prompt templates and a recommended redaction default (replace PII patterns with tokens but keep service identifiers) and a short human-review checklist for edge cases?

I’ll coordinate timelines with PaperTrail. If we can get initial pass results by EOD Fri next week (Sep 7), we can present during the next call.

Onward—
Connor

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ali Hassan <ali@papertrail.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: model suitability pack & prompt samples requested

Connor / team / Ali —

Got the files and started a quick run. Notes so far: 

- Micro-benchmark: ran 20 curated queries vs redwood-8k-llm-v2 (q4_0) and redwood-xl-16k (full fp16) on a dedicated instance. Attached preliminary latency/cost sheet (benchmark-results-20280829.pdf).
- Latency: redwood-8k (q4_0) 95th ~280ms in our isolated run; redwood-xl-16k (fp16) 95th ~640ms (expected).
- Quality: on 120 labeled items redwood-8k (q4_0) achieved 0.84 precision for short-answer extraction; failure modes concentrated on truncated logs and obfuscated tokens.

Immediate recommendations: 
1) Start with redwood-8k-llm-v2 (q4_0) for cost-sensitive routes and use redwood-xl-16k as a fallback for long-context debugging queries.
2) Default temperature 0.1; enforce answer-length constraint and confidence thresholding (we’ll include prompt scaffolding to elicit short, factual answers).

Next steps I’ll take:
- Produce the final suitability pack document with a small FAQ for redaction and a short human-review checklist for the 8 edge-case types. I’ll link the final report in HubSpot and Drive.
- Marissa: can you author the prompt templates and the exact redaction regexes? I can include them in the report.

Ali — I’ll post the final pack into the shared drive by COB Mon (Sep 3). Let us know if you want a quick walkthrough call.

Best,
Ben Carter
ML Infra Lead | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: benchmark-results-20280829.pdf
